guard.recoveryRule: Inspect the actual private receipt and live guard first. Resolve any attempted/unknown session before another login. Closed no-session preparation can be replaced with a fresh empty context.

authorization.source: Direct user selection: Authorize isolated npm login
authorization.expiredPreloginGuard: closed with no session created; fresh empty context permitted before login

authentication.outcome: Guarded CLI login did not establish an owned token. Operator subsequently clarified that only website login completed, without CLI authorization.

operatorLoginReport.interpretation: User reports successful login; whether the isolated CLI session completed remains unresolved.

operatorLoginClarification.selectedMeaning: Signed into npm in the browser, but did not complete an approval for CLI access.
operatorLoginClarification.assurance: Operator-reported absence of completed CLI authorization; not an independently observed server revocation.

operatorObservation.selectedMeaning: Signed into npm in the browser, but did not complete an approval for CLI access.
operatorObservation.assurance: Operator-reported absence of completed CLI authorization; not an independently observed server revocation.

revocation.closureBasis: Operator reports no completed CLI authorization; owned empty local context removed. No independent server invalidation claim.

limits: Readiness is a timestamped observation, not a promise the guard remains alive after idle/deadline or process loss.
Native browser web authentication is supported; unexpected legacy password/classic-code prompts stop without relaying credentials to chat.
SIGKILL, machine loss and unreachable provider are unresolved until cleanup-first recovery proves the real outcome.
Artifact approval does not authorize authentication or publication.

publicationRouteRequest.source: Direct user custom response at fresh CLI-login gate
publicationRouteRequest.statement: I want to authorize pubblication via CI
publicationRouteRequest.trustedPublisherPrerequisite: npm trust requires the package already to exist; initial-version OIDC support remains an open npm issue.
publicationRouteRequest.proposedBootstrapAuthentication: One-operation granular npm token with target-scope package-write access and publishing 2FA bypass, protected GitHub environment secret, immediate revocation/deletion after the attempt.
publicationRouteRequest.stableCandidateApprovalUnchanged: Still requires a fresh CI build and actual digest-bound approval.
